observation: Two ordinary wheel builds of the same source produced different archive SHA-256 values because ZIP member timestamps were not normalized. Their installed package identity and generated evidence were identical. Neither wheel was uploaded in the blocked browser attempt.
hypothesized_cause: The Python wheel container includes build-time ZIP timestamps even when its source members and installed semantics are unchanged.
change: Select a durable SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=1792321200 build as the sole P0v4 upload candidate, store it in the repository evidence directory, and update the notebook to require its exact SHA-256. Preserve the earlier temporary and ordinary builds as non-uploaded packaging observations.
predicted_effect: Future rebuilds using the same fixed epoch can be byte-compared, the upload payload survives temporary-directory cleanup, and the notebook cannot silently install a semantically matching but byte-different wheel.
discriminating_experiment: Install the durable wheel without dependencies under both admitted runtime pairs and require the generated arrays, summary and manifest hashes to match each other and the prior v4 verification before upload.
